full_judgment:
15. It is evident that under section 5(4) in the case of suit for sale on the basis of a mortgage, as is the case in the present instance, a preliminary decree shall become final upon an auction sale taking place and concomitantly the right to redemption shall be deemed to come to an end at that point in time. It is clear from the law that until such auction sale and final decree, the right to redeem remains intact. Applied in conjunction with section 33(7), however, that deeming provision of section 5(4) may very well be argued to meet its limitation in the circumstances envisaged in section 33(7) given that the fact or concept of on auction sale does not arise in a section 33(7) scenario. In that scenario, the very issuance of a section 33(7) Certificate of Title and its registration thereof may be construed as in itself tantamounting to a finality, thereby, extinguishing a right of redemption at the point of such issuance; The Petitioners and the Added Respondent No.3 respond to that line of thinking by satisfactorily stressing that the right to redeem is in fact a substantive right to property which ought not to be extinguished by mere implication given that section 33(7) remains silent on the extinguishment of the capacity to redeem inherent in any mortgagor. It is pointed out that this question of redemption could also have been better understood should section 5(4) have borne express reference to the status of a right of redemption in the context of section 33(7). But clearly section 5(4) bears no such reference to section 33(7). It is, accordingly, aptly argued that absent the specific declaration of the law extinguishing the right of redemption on the issuance of a section 33(7) Certificate of Title, it would be misconceived to expressly find on such extinguishment to the detriment of a mortgagor and this would go beyond the rules of either statutory interpretation or construction. This Court finds merit in these submissions as also explain the rationale behind this Court's Orders both of 2-5-2012 in Writ Petition No. 4591 of 2012 and of 30-7-2013 in the present Writ Petition. These two Orders properly read are found, accordingly, to extend to the Petitioners an opportunity to redeem the mortgage upon satisfaction of the Bank's outstanding claims in its totality. 

 16. This Court is of the view that a transfer of title under section 33(7) does not indeed envisage the right of foreclosure. In the scheme of the Act, foreclosure in the sense of a limitation on the right of redemption can only arise when associated with an auction sale contemplated in section 5(4). Beyond that, section 37(7) appears to this Court to operate independently of section 5(4) and the provisions in section 33(7) in not contemplating a transfer by sale must be found also not to envisage the existence of the corresponding right of foreclosure. This Court finds that resultantly, therefore, the fight of redemption under section 33(7) is always found to be alive and extant. It is that understanding of the law that this Court finds informs all relevant Orders of this Court in both these Writ Petitions seeking the Petitioners initiative to meet the Bank's outstanding claims to the fullest notwithstanding the issuance of a section 33(7) Certificate of Title.
